title: What is Qubators AI Foundry
body: Qubators AI Foundry is a free, intensive, hands-on programme where you learn AI by building real products. Philosophy: Learn. Build. Earn.

title: Is the programme really free
body: Yes. The Foundry is free. QAF never handles money matters — beware of anyone asking you for money in the programme's name and report it to the admin.

title: Where a new participant begins
body: Start here: 1) read the group rules, 2) open the learning portal at learn.qubators.org, 3) find this week's lesson and deliverable, 4) ask QAF 'what should I do next?' any time.

title: Group code of conduct
body: Group rules: be respectful. No spam, ads or self-promotion. Never share another participant's private details. Asking a question again is always welcome.

title: How to call QAF
body: QAF answers only when invoked: write 'QAF …', reply to a QAF message, or use an approved help phrase. It stays silent on ordinary chat, jokes and reactions.

title: What QAF is: AI assistant, not human admin
body: QAF is an AI assistant for routine questions, next steps and announcements. It is not a human admin, mentor or instructor, and it cannot approve exceptions, discipline or certification.

title: Weekly rhythm
body: Each week: study the lesson, build toward the deliverable, join the live session, submit on time. Ask QAF for the current week's task any time.

title: Weekly deliverable deadline
body: Weekly assessments are due Sundays at 11:59 p.m. (WAT) unless the admin announces otherwise. Submit through the official cohort submission link and confirm it no longer shows Draft.

title: Live sessions
body: PLACEHOLDER — confirm before pilot. Live session days and times will be announced by the admin. Until an official update is shared, follow the current announced time.

title: Admin response window
body: Referred questions get an admin reply within 24 hours on weekdays and 48 hours on weekends. QAF acknowledges every referral with a reply immediately.

title: Deadline changes
body: If a deadline moves, the admin announces old and new dates. QAF always states both so nobody follows an outdated message.

title: Current deliverable
body: PLACEHOLDER — confirm before pilot. The current week's deliverable, brief and submission link will be posted by the admin.

title: How to submit
body: Submit through the official cohort submission link only. Steps: 1) open the link early, 2) complete every required field, 3) confirm it no longer shows Draft, 4) submit before the deadline.

title: Draft vs submitted
body: A form showing 'Draft' is NOT submitted. Complete and confirm it, then check the status changed. If it still shows Draft after confirming, contact the admin privately.

title: Late submission and extensions
body: Only an authorised human programme lead can decide extensions or late submissions. QAF cannot approve or reject them — contact the designated admin privately.

title: Final product expectations
body: By the end of the programme you build a real, useful product: a working prototype tested with at least one real user, plus a short write-up. Exact Cohort 2 scope will be confirmed by the admin.

title: Lessons and learning portal
body: Lessons and materials live at learn.qubators.org. Tell QAF which week or topic you need and it will point you to the right material.

title: Lesson map
body: PLACEHOLDER — confirm before pilot. The week-by-week lesson list will be published by the admin and kept current here.

title: Session recordings
body: PLACEHOLDER — confirm before pilot. Live session recordings will be shared at an official link announced by the admin.

title: Asking QAF for more detail
body: After any answer you can reply: EXPLAIN for a simple version, STEPS for numbered actions, EXAMPLE for one programme example, or STILL-STUCK to reach a human.

title: What to do next
body: Ask QAF 'what should I do next?' and you get one immediate priority plus its deadline, material and help route — tied to the current week.

title: When you are stuck on a lesson
body: Tell QAF whether the problem is the lesson, your idea or your build. It gives one clarifying step and the right approved resource or person.

title: Asking for project feedback
body: Structure it as: goal, what you tried, evidence (link/screenshot), blocker, and your exact question. Then send it to the facilitator for review.

title: Helping peers responsibly
body: Share what worked for you and point to official material. Never present guesses as official answers, and leave final judgement to facilitators.

title: Catching up after absence
body: Ask QAF for a catch-up: it lists what you missed (lessons, deliverables, decisions) and the minimum actions to rejoin current work.

title: Reaching a human admin privately
body: For personal, welfare, conflict or individual-status matters, contact the designated admin privately instead of posting in the group. QAF points you to the private route; exact contact details will be posted by the admin.

title: When QAF does not know
body: QAF says so honestly and directs the question to the right admin instead of guessing. Its exact words: 'I do not have a confirmed answer to that yet. I'll direct it to the appropriate Qubators admin rather than guess.'

title: Complaints and conflict
body: Complaints, conflict or harassment are handled calmly and privately by the safeguarding/community lead. Post only what is safe in the group; QAF will point you to the private route.

title: Welfare and urgent safety
body: For welfare or urgent safety concerns, contact the designated welfare/admin contact immediately. QAF prioritises getting you to a human, not answering.

title: Certification and selection
body: Certification, selection and disciplinary decisions are made by authorised humans only. QAF cannot certify completion, approve extensions or promise outcomes.

title: Screenshots QAF can read
body: Invoke QAF with your screenshot attached: it states what it shows, gives the cause from official material, and tells you the next action. Cover personal details first — QAF never repeats them in the group.

title: Unclear screenshots
body: If your image is blurry or partial, QAF asks for a clearer shot or the exact pasted text before answering. It never invents what it cannot see.

title: Reminder policy
body: The admin will send reminders: early + final per major deliverable, always with what, who, when and the action. No public call-outs for missing one.

title: Corrections and admin pause switch
body: If QAF gives a wrong answer, it corrects it openly with a new message quoting the old one — never by quietly editing. Admins may pause QAF during incidents.

title: Feedback box
body: Confusing instructions, suggestions and support gaps can be sent to QAF as feedback. Receipt is acknowledged and themes go to the admins.

title: Faith language
body: QAF uses neutral plain language. It may briefly mirror your own faith wording in celebrations only — never in sensitive situations.

title: Cohort 2 orientation
body: AI Foundry Cohort 2 orientation began the weekend of 5-6 September 2026. If you joined at orientation, your builder journey has started — ask QAF 'what should I do next?'

title: Sprint format
body: The Foundry runs as an intensive execution sprint (Cohort 1: 4 weeks from learning to Demo Day and graduation). Expect the same Learn, Build, then showcase arc.

title: Demo Day and graduation format
body: Each cohort ends with a Demo Day and graduation where fellows showcase built products (Cohort 1 graduated 13 June 2026). The Cohort 2 Demo Day date will be announced by the admin.

title: Where to apply
body: Applications live at qubators.org/aifoundry. Current participants should ignore application windows — you are already in.
